title: Il Congiuntivo Imperfetto
subtitle: The subjunctive's past tense, used after a past-tense main clause.
objectives: Conjugate regular verbs in the congiuntivo imperfetto
Apply the sequence-of-tenses rule with a past-tense main verb
Recognize essere's fully irregular imperfect subjunctive

content.intro: When the main clause is in a past tense, the subjunctive in the subordinate clause shifts back too — into the congiuntivo imperfetto.
content.explanation: Formed regularly for almost every verb, including most that are irregular elsewhere: drop -re from the infinitive, add the endings. Only essere has a genuinely irregular stem (fossi, fossi, fosse...).

rules.heading: b) Sequence of tenses (simplified)
rules.body: Main clause in the present/future → subordinate in the congiuntivo presente. Main clause in a past tense or the conditional → subordinate in the congiuntivo imperfetto: Pensavo che avesse ragione. (I thought he was right.)

examples.en: I thought you had already left.
I was hoping you'd come to the party.

examples.it: Non credevo che fosse così difficile.
examples.en: I didn't think it would be so difficult.

examples.it: Volevo che tu sapessi la verità.
examples.en: I wanted you to know the truth.
It was important that everyone understood.

commonMistakes.why: A past-tense main verb (pensavo) requires the congiuntivo imperfetto, not the congiuntivo presente.
Volere che always requires the subjunctive, regardless of tense — here, the imperfect subjunctive.

items.prompt: "I wanted you to understand" — Volevo che tu ___

items.explanation: Regular congiuntivo imperfetto of sapere: sapessi.
Regular congiuntivo imperfetto of arrivare: arrivassero.

items.prompt: Which is essere's io form in the congiuntivo imperfetto?
items.explanation: Essere's imperfect subjunctive is fossi, fossi, fosse...

items.prompt: A past-tense main clause requires which subjunctive tense in the subordinate clause?
items.explanation: The sequence-of-tenses rule shifts the subjunctive back to the imperfetto.

items.statement: Only essere has a genuinely irregular stem in the congiuntivo imperfetto.
items.explanation: Almost every other verb follows the regular -assi/-essi pattern.

summary: Only essere is irregular: fossi, fossi, fosse, fossimo, foste, fossero.
A past-tense (or conditional) main clause requires the imperfect subjunctive in the subordinate clause.
